title: Why Don’t We See Any Research Reports About What Marijuana Prohibition Is “Linked To”?

content_html_sanitized:
For the last fifty years or so I have been reading about the “Latest Research”!!!! that says that cannabis is “linked to” something or other unpleasant.

 

I’m always appreciative of health advice, but the journalistic problem is that these reports are almost always presented with unquestioning reverence more appropriate for Church bulletins.

 

Unfortunately, these reports aren’t being used for health advice, but rather they are used as justification for harsh penalties for cannabis possession or to keep it in the black market.

 

Even worse, they have also been used to justify banning medical cannabis, even to those who are obviously suffering. Even disabled Veterans

 

But what else is “Marijuana Prohibition” actually “linked to”? Well, most cruelly, seriously disabled veterans are still having a difficult time getting access to medical cannabis, and especially through the Veterans Administration.

See

Veterans Who Fought for Our Freedom May Finally Get Medical Cannabis

And

The Wall Street Journal Carries Excellent Story About The Outrageous Medical Abuse of Veterans: But No Mention of Medical Cannabis

And from 2000

Disabled Vet and Wife Held at Gunpoint By Narks Who Seize Their Medical Marijuana Plants. In Washington State, Which Has A Medical Marijuana Law.

 

Oh, I almost forgot, like the media, there have been more than 30 million arrests in the last fifty years, and still another 200,000 every year.

See

30 Million Marijuana Arrests and Counting – Enough is Enough!

And

The Perils of Potent Pot Party Line: Blaming Marijuana Legalization for Increase in THC Levels

 

To quote my late, great friend, William F. Buckley, Jr.

“One of the problems that the marijuana reform movement consistently faces is that everyone wants to talk about what marijuana does, but no one ever wants to look at what marijuana prohibition does. Marijuana never kicks down your door in the middle of the night. Marijuana never locks up sick and dying people, does not suppress medical research, does not peek in bedroom windows. Even if one takes every reefer madness allegation of the prohibitionists at face value, marijuana prohibition has done far more harm to far more people than marijuana ever could."
